long_biography.plain_text:
Counter-Strike sessions in Copenhagen exposed Jacob Wolff-Petersen to a practical frustration: dust and wear made conventional mousepads inconsistent. He answered with Icemat, a precision glass surface, and turned that product into SteelSeries. The company grew by making hardware and software for professional and enthusiast gamers, while relationships with esports teams kept product development close to demanding users.

After outside investors joined, Wolff-Petersen moved from day-to-day leadership toward board-level product and strategic work, later reinvesting alongside Axcel. SteelSeries eventually became part of GN Store Nord. He now owns a Danish holding company that manages investments and has backed younger technology and consumer businesses. Those activities broaden his current portfolio, but gaming peripherals remain the defining foundation of his wealth and public identity over two decades.

uncertainties.detail: The Coast Guard and maritime sources identify SW Marine Limited as the registered owner of Seawolf X, while a Malta company-data reproduction names Jacob Wolff-Petersen as shareholder of that exact company. Direct access to the official Malta registry entry was not available, so the beneficial ownership link carries a small residual source-chain limitation despite the exact uncommon name and April 2022 timing match.

Wolff-Petersen currently owns a holding company whose registered purpose includes investments and which holds several operating interests. Public records do not disclose the full portfolio or his daily responsibilities, so Finance & Investments is classified with high rather than very-high confidence and should not obscure technology as the wealth-creation industry.

GN disclosed an enterprise value for SteelSeries, and filings establish that Wolff-Petersen reinvested before the later acquisition. The reviewed sources do not disclose his exact ownership percentage at closing, personal proceeds or current net worth; the dossier therefore makes no calculation from the company transaction value.

No reliable public source was found for a middle name, secondary nationality, exact birthplace, birth day or birth month. The upstream 1973 birth year is retained only as input context, and no unsupported missing field is proposed.

The existing LinkedIn profile matches the exact name and Copenhagen business identity. No verified personal Instagram or personal website was found. SteelSeries' official history page is proposed as the company website; no Forbes social is proposed because no dedicated profile was located.

The upstream biography is already populated and includes age and transaction-value language that can date quickly. Under the missing-field proposal contract it is not re-proposed; the dossier biographies provide durable, complementary editorial drafts for review.

Vessel and corporate-ownership records are used only to resolve the upstream identity. Seawolf X, its specifications and charter activity do not explain Wolff-Petersen's wealth mechanism and are excluded from both biographies and industry classifications.
